Indian Medical Insurance Corporation (IMIC) – Azure PaaS Deployment 

**1\. Overview** 

This submission describes a PaaS-only Azure deployment for Indian Medical Insurance Corporation. 

**2\. Users & Entry** 

*   Policy Holder – internet user (read-heavy) 
*   Insurance Agent – internet user (write-heavy, uploads) 
*   Company Staff – intranet/backend approvals 
*   Azure Front Door (WAF) – single secure ingress; routes to Web/API apps 

**3\. Core PaaS Components** 

*   Azure App Service – Web Apps (role-based portals) 
*   Azure App Service – API App (business logic) 
*   Azure API Management (APIM) – policy, throttling, versioning 
*   Azure SQL Database – transactional store 
*   Azure Blob Storage – documents (reports, bills) 
*   Azure Service Bus – async approvals & notifications 
*   Azure Notification Hubs/Email – outbound notifications 
*   Azure CDN – caches static content from Blob or App Service for global delivery 

**4\. End-to-End Flow** 

1.  User hits Front Door; WAF checks; request forwarded. 
2.  Dynamic pages served by Web App; API App handles business logic. 
3.  SQL/Blob handle data & documents; Service Bus decouples approvals. 
4.  Event triggers notification; email sent via Notification service. 
5.  Static assets are fetched via CDN (nearest PoP) for faster delivery. 

**5\. Benefits for Competition Scoring** 

*   Performance: Global acceleration via CDN; edge caching. 
*   Security: Front Door WAF + APIM policies; secrets in Key Vault (assumed). 
*   Scalability: Auto-scale App Service; CDN offloads static traffic. 
*   Reliability: Async workflows with Service Bus; monitored via App Insights. 
*   Cost: PaaS-managed services; pay-as-you-go; CDN reduces egress from origin.
